name: breadcrumb
title: Breadcrumb
description: The trail from the root to the current page.
docs:
## When to use - A hierarchy deeper than two levels, where the user needs to know where they are and how to get back up: `Workspace / Projects / cadence-ui`. - A page reached through a drill-down — a file inside a folder inside a drive. - A trail that doubles as navigation: every ancestor is a link, the current page is not. ## When not to use - Two levels of depth. The header already links home; a trail of two items adds noise. - A wizard or a multi-step form. That is a progress indicator, and it must not let the user jump to a step they have not reached. - A history of where the user came from ("back to search results"). That is a back link, and it should look like one. ## Installation ```bash npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/breadcrumb ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Breadcrumb, BreadcrumbItem, BreadcrumbLink, BreadcrumbList, BreadcrumbPage, BreadcrumbSeparator, } from "@/components/cadence/breadcrumb/breadcrumb"; export function Trail() { return ( Home plan.pdf ); } ``` ## Examples ### A deep trail that collapses `BreadcrumbEllipsis` stands in for the middle of a long path. Put a menu trigger next to it — the ellipsis itself is not interactive. ```tsx ``` ### A custom separator `BreadcrumbSeparator` takes any child; without one it renders a chevron at `size-3.5`. ```tsx / ``` ### A router link `BreadcrumbLink` takes Base UI's `render`, so the framework's own link component keeps its prefetching and client-side navigation. The `data-slot` survives the swap. ```tsx }>Files ``` ## API | Part | Props | Notes | | ---------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | | `Breadcrumb` | native nav props | `aria-label="breadcrumb"`. | | `BreadcrumbList` | native ol props | Flex row that wraps; muted, small text. | | `BreadcrumbItem` | native li props | Inline flex, one gap. | | `BreadcrumbLink` | `render`, anchor props| Anchor by default; `data-slot="breadcrumb-link"`. | | `BreadcrumbPage` | native span props | The current page: `aria-current="page"`, not a link. | | `BreadcrumbSeparator` | native li props | `role="presentation"`, `aria-hidden`; chevron by default. | | `BreadcrumbEllipsis` | native span props | Hidden from assistive tech; contains `sr-only` "More". | ## Motion contract No motion (T0). Nothing in a trail animates. A navigation landmark that fades or slides in is harder to find, and a trail that reflows on navigation makes the one stable thing on the page move. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- | | – | none | – | – | | reduced | none | – | – | | none | none | – | – | `transition-colors` on the link is hover feedback on the text colour only. ## Accessibility - The `nav` is labelled "breadcrumb", so it becomes its own landmark; a page may have several `nav`s and this is how they are told apart. - Order matters: `
    `/`
  1. ` gives the trail a length and a sequence, which is what a screen reader announces ("list, 3 items"). - The last item is `BreadcrumbPage`: `aria-current="page"`, `aria-disabled="true"`, and not focusable. It is where the user already is, so linking it is a no-op that costs a tab stop. - Separators are decorative — `role="presentation"` and `aria-hidden` — so the trail is read as names, not as "chevron". - An ellipsis must not be the only way to reach the hidden ancestors: pair it with a menu, or the collapsed path becomes unreachable. ## Notes for AI - Do not wrap the current page in a link "for consistency". It is a `BreadcrumbPage`. - Do not put the trail in a `Card` header as decoration; it is navigation and belongs near the top of the content region. - If the hierarchy is generated from a route, derive the trail from the route's segments rather than hand-writing items — a trail that disagrees with the URL is worse than none.
